metric: Debian popcon sourcemax installations by source package (pinned snapshot)
note: Leads are not verified parsers. Ranks are assigned only among verified paths.

leads.name: sqlite3
leads.reason: SQLite engine. sqlite3_prepare_v2 compiles statement text into a VDBE bytecode program; the documented C API exposes no syntax tree, so it does not give the AST summary. It is the oracle cross-check in controls/sql/check_controls.py, not a parser path.

leads.name: postgresql-18
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: PostgreSQL server source package; the server parser (raw_parser) is not a documented library API outside the backend. libpg_query is the extracted library form of this grammar.

leads.name: sqlcipher
leads.reason: SQLite fork with encryption; same engine API and no syntax tree, as for sqlite3.

leads.name: libgda5
leads.reason: GNOME Data Access 5. Its documented GdaSqlParser (gda_sql_parser_parse_string) returns a GdaStatement whose GdaSqlStatement contents are a public struct tree (select targets, FROM targets and joins, WHERE expression, GROUP BY, ORDER BY). Qualifies on documentation; not yet run. Its popcon count covers the whole data-access library, not SQL parsing. Not run in this round: a scoped source build of libgda (GLib/GObject, libxml2) under coverage and AFL++ was not attempted; it outranks the selected libpg_query by this metric and remains the next C lead.

leads.name: libpg-query
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: libpg_query: documented pg_query_parse / pg_query_parse_protobuf return the PostgreSQL parse tree (JSON or protobuf) for local text.

leads.name: duckdb
leads.reason: C++ library (DuckDB engine); recorded in the C++ cell.
